thread:
ashley: paging: canary deploy to prod triggered repeated crashloops and a partial node cordon during rolling drain. Customers seeing 503s to inference endpoints. oncall-bot: @pagerduty triggered · Severity: P1 · Acknowledged by ravi.

ravi: picking this up — oncall here. seeing a flurry of PodCrashLoopBackOffs for inference-canary-*/replica set. HPA also scaled up then pods failed readiness so requests got routed to fewer nodes.

maria: I can reproduce in staging with the canary manifest we pushed this morning — podAntiAffinity + requiredDuringScheduling causing pods to bunch and fail scheduling when we cordon nodes.

sam: logs from crashloop: ``ERROR: kv-cache init failed: can't mmap /var/lib/model/weights: permission denied`` — looks like initContainer mount/uid change?

leila: we changed a securityContext in the Helm chart to run as non-root for canary only. Could be a mount permission regression.

ravi: customer impact: small subset of requests hit canary and backed off; overall 10-15% increased 5xx from EU region. Not full outage but degraded for paying customers.

oncall-bot: Handoff triggered — current oncall: ravi. Next oncall standby: sam.

maria: snippet of problematic section in the canary chart: ```yaml
        affinity:
          podAntiAffinity:
            requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
              - labelSelector:
                  matchExpressions:
                    - key: app
                      operator: In
                      values: [inference]
                topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
        securityContext:
          runAsUser: 1001
          fsGroup: 1001
```

sam: also HPA spec for canary scaled minReplicas: 0 -> 3, targetCPU 60. When cordon happened hpa kept trying to create pods but they failed scheduling and kubelet spammed.

ashley: immediate mitigation options: 1) flip canary feature flag off (quick), 2) rollback canary deploy to previous chart (safer), 3) emergency patch to securityContext/mount perms (risky). Thoughts? :thinking_face:

leila: feature flag kill-switch is fastest. If we flip, traffic stops routing to canary and 503 spike should drop within a couple seconds.

ravi: agree. sam — can you run the kill switch now and confirm routing?

sam: running prod feature flag toggle: ``/ff toggle canary-inference routing false --env=prod`` — executed. Waiting for propagation.

sam: confirmed: no new canary pods are receiving traffic. Observability: 5xx rate dropping. :white_check_mark:

ashley: good. next: do we want rollback or patch and re-deploy? We should plan a rollback for the canary release and a postmortem.

maria: I think rollback chart -> previous tag is safe. I'll prepare helm rollback for the canary release and coordinate drain unblock.

sam: runbook step: uncordon any nodes we cordoned for drain unless drain still needed. Check for nodes with taint: ``kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.spec.taints}\\n'``

ravi: I'm escalating to infra to confirm no underlying disk/mount regressions. Not seeing cluster-wide fs errors, looks specific to canary mount path set in chart.

maria: executing rollback: ``helm rollback inference-canary 2 --namespace=prod`` — rolling it back to previous stable release.

oncall-bot: deploy bot: rollback started by maria. Tracking deploy id: dep-2026-03-15-0892.

maria: rollback completed. Pods now at stable image and securityContext reverted.

sam: kubectl shows stable pods running and readiness passing. No new CrashLoopBackOffs.

ashley: monitoring dashboards show 5xx back to baseline over last 3 minutes. Customer support notified.

ravi: assigned follow-ups: (1) root cause: misaligned securityContext + mount perms in canary chart (maria + leila), (2) HPA/canary interplay doc + safer minReplicas policy (sam), (3) add preflight checks to CI to validate mount perms for non-root (ashley).

leila: I'll open the postmortem and add timeline and remediation. Adding action item: require non-root runs to be smoke tested on staging with real volume mounts.

ashley: any outstanding customer-facing issues? cust-succ bot: created incident ticket INC-2026-331 for affected customers in EU, CS notified.

ravi: closing the page for now — monitoring for 30 mins. If we see regression we'll reopen. Thanks team. :pray:
